extracted.intended_audience: journalists, journalism students, and media professionals
extracted.subtask_description: A field-level code of ethics for journalists and news organizations that sets overarching values and 35 specific principles guiding reporting, sourcing, conflicts of interest, harm minimization, and accountability across all media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth and Report It
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalism should be accurate and fair. Journalists should be honest and courageous in gathering, reporting and interpreting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overarching principle. See the 18 specific practices under this heading (e.g., verify information, use original sources, identify sources clearly, avoid distortion, label commentary). The code says to read principles as a whole and not take individual parts out of context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalism treats sources, subjects, colleagues and members of the public as human beings deserving of respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overarching principle. See the 7 specific practices under this heading (e.g., balance public's need for information against harm, show compassion, consider cultural differences, weigh publication of personal information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest and primary obligation of ethical journalism is to serve the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overarching principle. See the 5 specific practices under this heading (e.g., avoid conflicts of interest, refuse gifts, distinguish news from advertising).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable and Transparent
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalism means taking responsibility for one’s work and explaining one’s decisions to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overarching principle. See the 5 specific practices under this heading (e.g., explain ethical choices, correct mistakes promptly, expose unethical conduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Take responsibility for the accuracy of their work
rubrics_metrics.description: Take responsibility for the accuracy of their work. Verify information before releasing it. Use original sources whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify facts proactively; prioritize original sources; accuracy is fundamental and primary over speed or format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neither speed nor format excuses inaccuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that neither speed nor format excuses inaccuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not sacrifice verification because of deadlines, breaking-news pressure, or platform constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context and avoid misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide context. Take special care not to misrepresent or oversimplify in promoting, previewing or summarizing a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure headlines, teasers, and summaries accurately reflect full reporting; avoid misleading framings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather, update and correct information throughout a story's life
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather, update and correct information throughout the life of a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat stories as living documents: update as new facts emerge and prominently correct earlier errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious when making promises and keep them
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious when making promises, but keep the promises they make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful about pledges to sources or subjects (e.g., about anonymity or off-the-record) and honor commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify sources clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources clearly. The public is entitled to as much information as possible to judge the reliability and motivations of sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose as much about sources' identity and motivations as is appropriate and safe, so audiences can assess credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider motives before granting anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider sources’ motives before promising anonymity. Reserve anonymity for sources who may face danger, retribution or other harm, and have information that cannot be obtained elsewhere. Explain why anonymity was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity should be exceptional, documented, and justified to the audience when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow subjects to respond to criticism or allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek subjects of news coverage to allow them to respond to criticism or allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make reasonable efforts to contact affected parties and include their perspective before publication when practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undercover or surreptitious methods unless necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information unless traditional, open methods will not yield information vital to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hidden reporting only when information is of high public importance and cannot be obtained openly; weigh ethical costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold power accountable and give voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable. Give voice to the voiceless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue oversight reporting and include marginalized perspectives to reflect the diversity and magnitude of human experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support open and civil exchange of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open and civil exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and present a range of viewpoints while maintaining standards of civility and factual accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve as watchdogs over public affairs and government
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to serve as watchdogs over public affairs and government. Seek to ensure that the public’s business is conducted in the open, and that public records are open to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize transparency in government and public institutions; pursue access to public records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide access to source material when relevant and appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to source material when it is relevant and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible and ethical, share documents, data, recordings or other source materials that support reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell diverse stories and seek seldom-heard voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Boldly tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience. Seek sources whose voices we seldom hear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively include diverse perspectives to avoid narrow or biased coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping. Journalists should examine the ways their values and experiences may shape their reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on implicit biases and guard against reductive portrayals of individuals or groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label advocacy and commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Label advocacy and commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly mark opinion, sponsored content, and advocacy to distinguish them from news reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never deliberately distort facts or context
rubrics_metrics.description: Never deliberately distort facts or context, including visual information. Clearly label illustrations and re-enactments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not manipulate images, audio, or video; make staging or reenactments explicit to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never plagiarize; always attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize. Always attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit all sources and materials properly; do not present others' work as your own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance public's need for information against potential harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance the public’s need for information against potential harm or discomfort. Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance or undue intrusiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh newsworthiness against privacy, dignity, and potential negative consequences for subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show compassion for those affected by coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Show compassion for those who may be affected by news coverage. Use heightened sensitivity when dealing with juveniles, victims of sex crimes, and sources or subjects who are inexperienced or unable to give consent. Consider cultural differences in approach and treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply additional care to vulnerable subjects and respect cultural norms and consent limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal access ≠ ethical justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that legal access to information differs from an ethical justification to publish or broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if information is legally obtainable, evaluate whether publishing it is ethically appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect greater privacy rights of private people
rubrics_metrics.description: Realize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than public figures and others who seek power, influence or attention. Weigh the consequences of publishing or broadcasting personal information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a higher threshold for intrusion into private individuals' lives versus public figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity, even if others do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist sensationalism and coverage that exploits victims or encourages voyeurism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance suspect's fair trial rights with public's right to know
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a suspect’s right to a fair trial with the public’s right to know. Consider the implications of identifying criminal suspects before they face legal charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider legal and ethical consequences of naming suspects; avoid prejudicial reporting that could affect judicial fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider long-term implications of permanence of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the long-term implications of the extended reach and permanence of publication. Provide updated and more complete information as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of how online permanence affects individuals; correct and update records when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest; disclose unavoidable conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived. Disclose unavoidable conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recuse or disclose when personal, financial, or other interests could influence coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse gifts, favors and special treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment, and avoid political and other outside activities that may compromise integrity or impartiality, or may damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject offers that could create influence or appearance of bias; maintain independence from subjects and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pay for access; identify paid content
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money; do not pay for access to news. Identify content provided by outside sources, whether paid or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid buying information that compromises integrity; disclose when content or contributions are paid or sponsored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny favored treatment to advertisers or special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers, donors or any other special interests, and resist internal and external pressure to influence coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect editorial independence from commercial or donor influence; ensure editorial decisions stand apart from revenue sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish news from advertising; label sponsored content
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two. Prominently label sponsored content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly separate editorial content from advertising, promotions, native ads, or sponsored features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain ethical choices and processes to audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain ethical choices and processes to audiences. Encourage a civil dialogue with the public about journalistic practices, coverage and news content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about methods, sourcing decisions, and trade-offs; invite constructive public engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond quickly to questions about accuracy, clarity and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond quickly to questions about accuracy, clarity and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have mechanisms to receive and reply to audience concerns promptly and respectfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and correct mistakes promptly and prominently
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge mistakes and correct them promptly and prominently. Explain corrections and clarifications carefully and clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make corrections visible and explanatory, not buried; document what changed and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose unethical conduct in journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical conduct in journalism, including within their organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and report breaches of journalistic ethics, including internal wrongdoing, and apply standards impartially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by the same high standards they expect of others
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards they expect of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold oneself and one's organization to the same ethical benchmarks applied to external subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Code is a guide, not legally enforceable rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPJ Code of Ethics is a statement of abiding principles ... It is not a set of rules, rather a guide that encourages all who engage in journalism to take responsibility for the information they provide, regardless of medium. The code should be read as a whole; individual principles should not be taken out of context. It is not, nor can it be under the First Amendment, legally enforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Code as a principled framework and judgment aid; consult additional resources and position papers for evolving practices.
